title: They looked the same.
paragraphs:
They looked the same.
Same temple. Same prayer. Same God.
But heaven rejected one… and justified the other.

Not the words.
Not the posture.
Not the performance.

Because what you hide behind your actions…
God sees clearly.

Because it means you can do the right things…
for the wrong reasons…
and still be far from Him.
Two men walked into the temple in Luke 18:9–14.

One stood tall. Clean. Impressive.
The kind of man people respect.
“God, I thank you that I am not like other men…” — Luke 18:11

He wasn’t talking to God—
he was talking about himself.

Comparison.
Pride.
Self-exaltation dressed up as worship.
Now look at the other man.

A traitor in the eyes of society.
Dirty reputation.
No religious résumé.
“God, be merciful to me, a sinner!” — Luke 18:13

No performance.
No polish.
No pretending.
“This man went down to his house justified, rather than the other.” — Luke 18:14
The “bad guy” walks away right with God?

Because God is not impressed with your image—
He’s after your heart.
“The Lord looks at the heart.” — 1 Samuel 16:7

You can serve in church… and still be serving yourself.
You can give… and secretly crave recognition.
You can post Bible verses… and be starving for applause.
You can lead… preach… sing… and still be building your own name.
And God sees the difference every single time.

Because suddenly you realize—
“Even my good works aren’t pure.”
“All our righteous acts are like filthy rags.” — Isaiah 64:6

Not just your sin—
even your best efforts are stained when they come from pride.
So where does that leave us?
Unable to impress a holy God.
And this is where everything pivots.

Because Christianity is not about perfecting your image—
it’s about surrendering your heart.
He didn’t come for the polished Pharisee.
He came for the broken tax collector.
“I have not come to call the righteous, but sinners to repentance.” — Luke 5:32

Your mixed motives don’t disqualify you—
but pretending they don’t exist does.
Jesus didn’t die for your performance.

The hidden pride.
The secret need for validation.
The quiet self-glory behind holy actions.
On the cross, He took it.

Not just what you’ve done—
but why you’ve done it.
And then He offers something radical:
“I will give you a new heart, and a new spirit I will put within you.” — Ezekiel 36:26
But it only happens one way:

Turn from self.
Turn from image.
Turn from pride.
And fall before Jesus like that tax collector:

When you come low—
He lifts you.

When you stop performing—
He starts transforming.

When you surrender the motive—
He purifies the heart.
“If we confess our sins, He is faithful and just to forgive us… and to cleanse us.” — 1 John 1:9
So let me ask you something real:
Why do you do what you do?

Not what people see.
Not what you post.
Not what you say out loud.

Because the same Jesus who exposed the Pharisee—
is the same Jesus who justified the sinner.
And He’s ready to do it again.

If you’re tired of performing…
if you’re exhausted from keeping up the image…
if you’re done pretending you’re okay—

And in that place—
grace meets you.

Not to shame you—
but to redeem you.
